environment_dependencies: C-based bare-metal test harness (test_common.h) providing write_reg, read_reg, wait_on, finish
GIC interrupt controller used (GIC_EnableIRQ, GIC_ClearIRQ) for IRQ lines 80 and 81
I2C register definitions (i2c_def.h / i2c0_def.h / i2c1_def.h, i2c_offset.h)
LSS SYSREG for interrupt routing and security configuration (lss_sysreg_def.h, lss_sysreg_offset.h)

execution_matrix.loops: For each of 6 patterns, write/verify across all 43 registers subject to masks and skips

execution_matrix.transfer_direction: Memory -> I2C0 (DMA CH0), I2C1 -> Memory (DMA CH1)
execution_matrix.synchronization: IRQ-based completion for I2C transfer; polling for DMA completion

execution_matrix.transfer_direction: Memory -> I2C0 (DMA CH0), I2C1 -> Memory (DMA CH1)
execution_matrix.synchronization: IRQ-based completion for I2C transfer; polling for DMA completion

risks: Registers with read/write masks of 0 cannot be accessed for the corresponding operation; incorrect expectations may cause false failures
Interrupt not occurring or not being cleared could stall the test waiting for int_pend to change
DMA completion detection relies on polling DMAC channel enable register; timing variations may extend wait durations
Hard-coded LSS NIC security configuration writes must succeed; otherwise peripheral access may be blocked
assumptions: The write_reg/read_reg/wait_on/finish/GIC_* APIs behave as expected by the test harness
LSS SYSREG address writes (0xA1700008..0xA1700054) correctly configure non-secure access for I2C and DMA paths
I2C interrupt line mapping to IRQ 80/81 is valid in the test environment
DMA source request codes (e.g., 0x5, 0x6) are correct for I2C0 TX and I2C1 RX paths respectively

testcases.Feature: Registers accessed by the processor through AHB interface
testcases.Test Description: Verifies default reset values and masked read/write behavior across the I2C register set via the processor interface. For each register, the test checks the default value and then exercises multiple data patterns while honoring read/write masks and skip rules, confirming that only writable and readable bits change and that preserved bits match defaults.
testcases.Remarks: Registers without read access are skipped for default checks. Registers without write access are skipped during pattern writes and subsequent reads. Addresses listed in the skip array are not accessed.
Test Steps / Procedure: Entry: Begin execution at the test entry point.

Default value verification phase: Iterate through the register list; for each address, if reading is allowed, read the register and compare with the expected default value; record a failure if there is a mismatch; skip addresses that are not readable.

Pattern write phase: For each data pattern in the predefined set, iterate through the register list and write the pattern to each address that is not skipped and that is writable; skip addresses marked to be skipped or not writable.

Pattern readback and validation phase: For each data pattern previously written, iterate through the register list and, for addresses that are not skipped and are both writable and readable, read back the value; compute the expected value by applying the read and write masks and preserving default bits where writing is disallowed; compare the readback to the computed expected value and record a failure on mismatch; skip addresses not permitted for read or write.
Completion: If any default-value or write/read mismatches were recorded, report failure; otherwise, report success.
Validation / Acceptance Criteria: Each readable register's value equals its expected default during the default check phase.

For each data pattern and for each address that is writable and readable, the readback value equals the expected value derived from mask logic (writable bits reflect the pattern; non-writable bits retain default values).
Final pass condition: No failures recorded in either default-value or write/read checks; the test completes with a zero status.
testcases.Hidden_Test_Description: Test exercises I2C register default values and read/write behavior using arrays from test_define.c. It calls chk_rst_val() then chk_rd_wr() from test_case(). Six data patterns are used. Fail counts (def_fail_cnt, wr_fail_cnt) determine finish(0/1).
testcases.Hidden_Remarks: Addresses with read_mask_array[i] == 0x00000000 are skipped for read. Addresses with write_mask_array[i] == 0x00000000 are skipped for write and also skipped for subsequent read verification. Addresses with skip_array[i] == 1 are skipped for both write and read phases.
Hidden_Test_Steps_Procedure: If (data_rd == default_value_array[i]) then PASS log (optional under DEBUG_DISPLAY) else def_fail_cnt++ and print failure with addr, expected, read.
If (data_rd == exp_val) PASS (optional log) else wr_fail_cnt++ and print mismatch with addr, expected, read.
Note: soft_reset_chk() is present but commented out; no delays are used in this test path.
testcases.Hidden_Validation_Acceptance_Criteria: PASS if and only if: (1) For all i where read_mask_array[i] != 0, read_reg(addr_array[i]) == default_value_array[i] in chk_rst_val(); (2) For all six patterns and all i where skip_array[i] == 0 and both write_mask_array[i] != 0 and read_mask_array[i] != 0, the read_reg(addr_array[i]) equals exp_val computed as ((data_wr & read_mask_array[i] & write_mask_array[i]) | ((write_mask_array[i] ^ 0xffffffff) & read_mask_array[i] & default_value_array[i])); (3) def_fail_cnt == 0 and wr_fail_cnt == 0 leading to finish(0).

testcases.Test Description: Configures I2C0 as master and I2C1 as slave, prepares DMA transfers to move data from memory to the transmit path and from the receive path to memory, sets clock count registers for high-speed timing, initiates a transfer and relies on an interrupt to signal completion, then verifies data integrity end-to-end.
testcases.Remarks: Security configuration writes are performed on the system register block before enabling interrupts. Two interrupt lines are enabled for the test. Interrupt masking leaves the transfer-complete source enabled. DMA completion is detected by polling the channel enable register until it is cleared. The wait loops include explicit delays.
Test Steps / Procedure: Entry: Begin at the test entry function for this scenario.
Security and system setup: Write to a sequence of system addresses to configure the interconnect for non-secure slave access.
Enable interrupts: Enable the two relevant interrupt lines in the interrupt controller.
Route and enable I2C interrupts in the system register block to allow I2C0 and I2C1 events.

I2C configuration: Clear pending I2C interrupts on both instances; program device control for both instances; set the slave address on I2C1 and the master’s target on I2C0; set the byte count on both; program standard-mode and high-speed clock count registers on the master as required; set the master code; mask all but the transfer-complete interrupt; set FIFO thresholds; and enable DMA on the master side.
Prepare transmit data: Initialize a small buffer of words in SRAM with a simple increasing pattern.

Configure DMA for memory-to-peripheral transfer: Program the channel control, source address, destination address, source count, source and destination address strides, source request code, and enable the channel.
Wait for DMA completion: Poll the channel enable register until it reads zero, inserting short waits between polls.
Start I2C transfer: Write to the transfer control register on the master to begin the transaction.
Poll transmit progress: Read the current byte-count register repeatedly until it reaches zero, inserting short waits between polls.
Wait for transfer-complete interrupt: Loop while the internal flag indicates pending; insert short waits until the interrupt handler clears the flag.

Initiate peripheral-to-memory DMA: Enable DMA on the slave side; configure the second channel to transfer from the slave data register to SRAM; set control and addressing parameters and enable the channel.
Wait for the second DMA completion: Poll the global channel enable register until clear, with short waits between polls.
Data integrity check: For each word, read the source SRAM word and the corresponding destination word and compare; record a failure if any mismatch is found.
Completion: Insert a brief delay, then report overall success or failure based on the accumulated error count.
Validation / Acceptance Criteria: During interrupt handling, the device interrupt status reflects a transfer-complete event and is successfully cleared; the corresponding system interrupt status is also cleared.
All transferred data words match exactly between the source SRAM region and the destination SRAM region.
Final pass condition: No errors recorded and the test completes with a zero status.
testcases.Hidden_Test_Description: I2C0 master to I2C1 slave DMA test. Sets LSS NIC non-secure, enables IRQ 80/81, enables LSS I2C interrupts, configures I2C0/I2C1, loads 5 words into SRAM starting at 0xA0243F00, configures DMA CH0 (mem->I2C0 SMB host block data), waits for DMA done by polling MIZAR_DMA_DMA_CH_EN, starts I2C transfer, polls MIZAR_I2C0_I2C_CURRENT_BYTECNT until 0, waits for Default_IRQHandler() to signal completion (int_pend=0), then enables I2C1 DMA and configures DMA CH1 (I2C1 SMB host block data->SRAM 0xA0243E00). After DMA completion, compares 5 words from both SRAM regions, delays, and calls finish(test_err).
testcases.Hidden_Remarks: System configuration writes at 0xA1700008..0xA1700054 set non-secure access. Only the transfer-complete interrupt (0x0010) is expected from I2C0. int_pend gate is set to 1 at start and cleared in Default_IRQHandler(). DMA completion is polled via MIZAR_DMA_DMA_CH_EN. TX byte countdown is polled via MIZAR_I2C0_I2C_CURRENT_BYTECNT.
Hidden_Test_Steps_Procedure: Security programming: write_reg(0xA1700008,0x1); write_reg(0xA170000C,0x1); write_reg(0xA1700014,0x1); write_reg(0xA1700018,0x1); write_reg(0xA170001C,0x1); write_reg(0xA1700020,0x1); write_reg(0xA1700024,0x1); write_reg(0xA1700028,0x1); write_reg(0xA170002C,0x1); write_reg(0xA1700030,0x1); write_reg(0xA1700034,0x1); write_reg(0xA1700038,0x1); write_reg(0xA170003C,0x1); write_reg(0xA1700044,0x1); write_reg(0xA1700048,0x1); write_reg(0xA1700050,0x1); write_reg(0xA1700054,0x1).
FIFO thresholds: write_reg(MIZAR_I2C0_TX_FIFO_THLD,0x5); write_reg(MIZAR_I2C1_TX_FIFO_THLD,0x5); write_reg(MIZAR_I2C0_RX_FIFO_THLD,0x5); write_reg(MIZAR_I2C1_RX_FIFO_THLD,0x5);
Data preload loop for i=0..4: tx_data[i]=i*5; write_reg(src_addr + 4*i, tx_data[i]);

DMA CH0 configuration (mem->I2C0): write_reg(MIZAR_DMA_CH0_CTRL,0x8028028); write_reg(MIZAR_DMA_CH0_SRC_ADDR,src_addr); write_reg(MIZAR_DMA_CH0_DEST_ADDR,dest_addr); write_reg(MIZAR_DMA_CH0_SRC_XCNT,0x5); write_reg(MIZAR_DMA_CH0_SRC_XMDFY,0x4); write_reg(MIZAR_DMA_CH0_DEST_XMDFY,0x0); write_reg(MIZAR_DMA_CH0_SRC_REQ,0x5); write_reg(MIZAR_DMA_DMA_CH_EN,0x1);
Poll current bytecount: do { data_rd = read_reg(MIZAR_I2C0_I2C_CURRENT_BYTECNT); wait_on(100); } while(data_rd != 0);

DMA CH1 configuration (I2C1->mem): write_reg(MIZAR_DMA_CH1_CTRL,0x8024028); write_reg(MIZAR_DMA_CH1_SRC_ADDR,src_addr); write_reg(MIZAR_DMA_CH1_DEST_ADDR,dest_addr); write_reg(MIZAR_DMA_CH1_SRC_XCNT,0x5); write_reg(MIZAR_DMA_CH1_SRC_XMDFY,0x0); write_reg(MIZAR_DMA_CH1_DEST_XMDFY,0x4); write_reg(MIZAR_DMA_CH1_SRC_REQ,0x6); write_reg(MIZAR_DMA_DMA_CH_EN,0x2);
Data compare loop for i=0..4: data_sent = read_reg(0xA0243F00 + 4*i); data_rcvd = read_reg(0xA0243E00 + 4*i); if(data_sent != data_rcvd) { test_err++; }

If (int_status == 0x0010) { write_reg(MIZAR_I2C0_INTR_CLR,0x00000010); GIC_ClearIRQ(80); GIC_ClearIRQ(81); write_reg(MIZAR_LSS_SYSREG_RAW_STCR0, LSS_SYSREG_RAW_STCR0_I2C0_INTERRUPT); wait_on(100); int_status = read_reg(MIZAR_I2C0_INTR_STS); int_status_lss = read_reg(MIZAR_LSS_SYSREG_RAW_STCR0) & LSS_SYSREG_INTR_EN0_I2C0_INTERRUPT; if (int_status != 0x00 || int_status_lss != 0x00) { test_err++; } } else { test_err++; }
testcases.Hidden_Validation_Acceptance_Criteria: PASS if: (1) In Default_IRQHandler(), read_reg(MIZAR_I2C0_INTR_STS) == 0x0010, and after write_reg(MIZAR_I2C0_INTR_CLR,0x00000010) and write_reg(MIZAR_LSS_SYSREG_RAW_STCR0, LSS_SYSREG_RAW_STCR0_I2C0_INTERRUPT), both read_reg(MIZAR_I2C0_INTR_STS) == 0x00 and (read_reg(MIZAR_LSS_SYSREG_RAW_STCR0) & LSS_SYSREG_INTR_EN0_I2C0_INTERRUPT) == 0x00; else test_err++. (2) For i=0..4, read_reg(0xA0243F00 + 4*i) == read_reg(0xA0243E00 + 4*i); else test_err++. (3) finish(test_err) is invoked with test_err == 0.

testcases.Test Description: Sets up I2C0 as master and I2C1 as slave for a standard‑mode transfer using DMA. Data is staged from memory to the transmit path and then captured from the receive path back to memory. The test waits for an interrupt to signal transfer completion and then verifies end‑to‑end data integrity.
testcases.Remarks: Security configuration writes are issued prior to enabling interrupts. Transfer-complete is the expected interrupt source. DMA completion is polled via the channel enable register. The polling loop for remaining bytes uses a longer wait duration.
Test Steps / Procedure: Entry: Begin at the test entry function for this scenario.
Security configuration: Write to the sequence of system addresses to allow non-secure access for the relevant interfaces.
Enable interrupts: Enable the two relevant lines in the interrupt controller.
Enable system-level I2C interrupts for both instances.

I2C configuration: Clear pending I2C interrupts; set device control values; configure the slave address on I2C1 and the target on I2C0; set the byte count on both; program standard-mode clock count registers on the master; mask all but the transfer-complete interrupt; set FIFO thresholds; enable DMA on the master.
Initialize transmit data: Populate a small buffer in SRAM with an increasing pattern.
Configure DMA channel for memory-to-peripheral movement: Set control and addressing registers and enable the channel.
Wait for DMA completion: Poll the channel enable register until it clears.
Start transfer: Write to the master’s transfer control register to begin.
Poll progress: Read the current byte-count register repeatedly until it becomes zero, inserting a longer wait between polls.
Wait for transfer-complete interrupt: Loop until the internal flag shows the interrupt has been serviced.
Configure peripheral-to-memory DMA: Enable DMA on the slave; set up control and addressing for the second channel and enable it.
Wait for second DMA completion: Poll the channel enable register until it is cleared.
Data integrity verification: Compare each word in the source and destination SRAM buffers; record any mismatches.
Finalize: Insert a brief delay and then report pass/fail based on accumulated errors.
Validation / Acceptance Criteria: The transfer-complete interrupt is observed and cleared successfully at both the device and system levels.
All data words written and received match exactly between the source and destination SRAM locations.
Final pass condition: No errors are recorded and the test returns a zero status.
testcases.Hidden_Test_Description: I2C0 master to I2C1 slave DMA standard-mode test. Sets LSS NIC non-secure, enables IRQ 80/81, enables LSS I2C interrupts, configures I2C0/I2C1, loads 5 words into SRAM at 0xA0243FC0, configures DMA CH0 (mem->I2C0), waits for DMA done, starts I2C transfer, polls MIZAR_I2C0_I2C_CURRENT_BYTECNT with wait_on(5000) until 0, waits for Default_IRQHandler() to clear int_pend, then enables I2C1 DMA and configures DMA CH1 (I2C1->SRAM at 0xA0243FE0). Compares the 5 words and calls finish(test_err).
testcases.Hidden_Remarks: System writes at 0xA1700008..0xA1700054 configure non-secure access. Only transfer-complete (0x0010) from I2C0 is expected. int_pend is set at start and cleared by Default_IRQHandler(). DMA completion is detected via MIZAR_DMA_DMA_CH_EN polling. The bytecount polling loop uses wait_on(5000).
Hidden_Test_Steps_Procedure: Security programming: write_reg(0xA1700008,0x1); write_reg(0xA170000C,0x1); write_reg(0xA1700014,0x1); write_reg(0xA1700018,0x1); write_reg(0xA170001C,0x1); write_reg(0xA1700020,0x1); write_reg(0xA1700024,0x1); write_reg(0xA1700028,0x1); write_reg(0xA170002C,0x1); write_reg(0xA1700030,0x1); write_reg(0xA1700034,0x1); write_reg(0xA1700038,0x1); write_reg(0xA170003C,0x1); write_reg(0xA1700044,0x1); write_reg(0xA1700048,0x1); write_reg(0xA1700050,0x1); write_reg(0xA1700054,0x1).
For i=0..4: tx_data[i] = i*5; write_reg(0xA0243FC0 + 4*i, tx_data[i]);

DMA CH0: write_reg(MIZAR_DMA_CH0_CTRL,0x8028028); write_reg(MIZAR_DMA_CH0_SRC_ADDR,src_addr); write_reg(MIZAR_DMA_CH0_DEST_ADDR,dest_addr); write_reg(MIZAR_DMA_CH0_SRC_XCNT,0x5); write_reg(MIZAR_DMA_CH0_SRC_XMDFY,0x4); write_reg(MIZAR_DMA_CH0_DEST_XMDFY,0x0); write_reg(MIZAR_DMA_CH0_SRC_REQ,0x5); write_reg(MIZAR_DMA_DMA_CH_EN,0x1);

DMA CH1: write_reg(MIZAR_DMA_CH1_CTRL,0x8024028); write_reg(MIZAR_DMA_CH1_SRC_ADDR,src_addr); write_reg(MIZAR_DMA_CH1_DEST_ADDR,dest_addr); write_reg(MIZAR_DMA_CH1_SRC_XCNT,0x5); write_reg(MIZAR_DMA_CH1_SRC_XMDFY,0x0); write_reg(MIZAR_DMA_CH1_DEST_XMDFY,0x4); write_reg(MIZAR_DMA_CH1_SRC_REQ,0x6); write_reg(MIZAR_DMA_DMA_CH_EN,0x2);
addr = 0xA0243FC0; addr1 = 0xA0243FE0; For i=0..4: data_sent = read_reg(addr); data_rcvd = read_reg(addr1); if(data_sent != data_rcvd) test_err++; addr += 4; addr1 += 4;

Default_IRQHandler(): same logic as hs_md: expect MIZAR_I2C0_INTR_STS == 0x0010, clear via MIZAR_I2C0_INTR_CLR and MIZAR_LSS_SYSREG_RAW_STCR0 write; verify both device and system interrupt states become 0; else test_err++.
testcases.Hidden_Validation_Acceptance_Criteria: PASS if: (1) Default_IRQHandler() observes MIZAR_I2C0_INTR_STS == 0x0010 and, after clearing, read_reg(MIZAR_I2C0_INTR_STS) == 0x00 and (read_reg(MIZAR_LSS_SYSREG_RAW_STCR0) & LSS_SYSREG_INTR_EN0_I2C0_INTERRUPT) == 0x00; else test_err++. (2) For i=0..4, read_reg(0xA0243FC0 + 4*i) == read_reg(0xA0243FE0 + 4*i); else test_err++. (3) finish(test_err) is called with test_err == 0.
